AMENDED
  CITY OF LA VERNE

  PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA

  Wednesday, June 22, 2022, 9:00 a.m.
  Watch Live at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750

The Public Financing Authority meeting for La Verne’s Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District will
be closed to the public in compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread
of the COVID-19 Virus. However, the public is encouraged to participate in this meeting in any of the
following ways:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream
  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They will be
  shared with the Authority Members prior to the meeting and will be made part of the permanent
  record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m. the day before the meeting.
  Please be advised that public comments submitted by emails or any other format to the
  City are public records that will be made available for public viewing.
  3) Participate on Zoom by registering here before 8:00 am the day of the meeting:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_Nuc6pPvyQeSm5HeYHlNpVg
  4) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may email
  planning@cityoflaverne.org by 8:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone number and
  the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate time during the
  meeting for your comment.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Assistant City
Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

 2.  Approval of Minutes – March 9, 2022

3.  Declaration of Emergency - Pursuant to Government Code Section 54953, the Public Financing
  Authority may continue to hold their public meetings via teleconference due to the COVID-19
  pandemic by adopting a resolution. Staff has prepared a resolution declaring the need to continue
  to meet teleconferencing at this time.

  Staff recommends that the Authority Board approve PFA Resolution No. 22-02 allowing for
  meetings to occur via teleconference.

4.  Public Hearing - Annual Report – Per State Law, the Public Financing Authority is required to
  adopt an annual report of activities undertaken within the last fiscal year. This is the second
  annual report of the District, and was mailed out to all property owners and participating taxing
  entities (County).

  Staff recommends that the Authority Board hold a public hearing on the annual report,
  taking any written or oral testimony, and approve PFA Resolution No. 22-03, adopting the
  submitted Annual Report for fiscal year 2021-2022.

5.  L Line and Development Updates – Staff will update the Authority Board on the progress of
  construction of the L Line and private development within or near the District.

  No action is required by the Authority Board.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS - This is the time set aside for anyone wishing
  to address the Public Financing Authority on items not listed in any other place on the agenda.
  Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or engaging
  in discussion on any item not appearing on the posted agenda. However, your concerns may be
  referred to staff or set for discussion at a later date. The Chair reserves the right to place limits on
  duration of comments.

7.  ADJOURNMENT – The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Public Financing Authority will
  be held on Wednesday, September 14, 2022 at 9:00 a.m., and is expected to be held virtually at
  www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

   PFA RESOLUTION NO. 22-02

A RESOLUTION OF THE LA VERNE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY (PFA)
FORMING ENHANCED INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING DISTRICT NO.1 MAKING
SPECIFIED FINDINGS TO ENABLE THE PFA TO CONTINUE TO HOLD MEETINGS
VIA TELECONFERENCING

  WHEREAS, AB 361 (Rivas), and specifically Government Code section 54953
(“Section 54953”), authorizes local agencies to use teleconferencing without complying
with the specified teleconferencing requirements imposed by the Ralph M. Brown Act
when the legislative body of a local agency holds a meeting during a declared state of
emergency and makes certain findings relating thereto; and

  WHEREAS, Section 54953 allows for local agencies to teleconference if the
legislative body finds, among other things, that state or local official continue to impose
or recommend measures to promote social distancing or whether a state of emergency
directly impacts the ability of the legislative body to meet safely and that meeting in
person would present imminent risks to the health and safety of attendees; and

  WHEREAS, on March 4, 2020, the Governor of California proclaimed a State of
Emergency to exist in California as result of the threat of COVID-19, which state of
emergency remains in place; and

  WHEREAS, on March 4, 2020, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors
and Los Angeles County Health Officer declared a local and health emergency as result
of the threat of COVID-19, which emergency remains in place; and

  WHEREAS, teleconferencing meetings enables the PFA to retain the ability to
continue to conduct meetings in a safe manner that would reduce exposure to members
and staff to COVID-19; and

  WHEREAS, public access and participation remain a core value of the PFA, and
the PFA has the capability to meet the requirements in Section 54953 to provide the
public with the ability to view, hear, and participate in such meetings in a manner that
protects the statutory and constitutional rights of all persons to participate in such
meetings; and

  WHEREAS, as a condition of extending the use of the provisions to conduct
remote teleconference meetings without compliance with specified Brown Act
teleconference requirements, the PFA must reconsider the circumstances of the state of
emergency that exists, and the PFA Board has done so.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the PFA Board does hereby find
the existence of a local and state of emergency in California caused by COVID-19
continues to directly impact the ability of the PFA to hold public meetings safely in
person and local and state health officials continue to recommend social distancing.

SUBJECT:  Annual Report and Finance Report
______________________________________________________________________

AGENDA SUMMARY

In accordance with Government Code Section 53398.66(j)(2) and (3), staff has prepared the annual
report for fiscal year 2021-2022 for the Public Financing Authority (PFA) of the Enhanced Infrastructure
Financing District (EIFD). The annual report is required to include the financial information from the
previous fiscal year. As a result of the way in which projects are being paid for through the City’s budget,
this agenda report will also detail those expenditures.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Authority Board conduct a public hearing on the Annual Report, taking any
written or verbal testimony, and then adopt PFA Resolution No. 22-03, adopting the report for the EIFD
for fiscal year 2021-2022.

BACKGROUND

State law requires that an Annual Report be approved for any Enhanced Infrastructure Financing
District (EIFD) through a public hearing process before the Public Finance Authority (PFA) of the EIFD.

The draft report was mailed out to all property owners within the EIFD area and posted to the District’s
website (www.cityoflaverne.org/eifd) as required. The report list projects that were undertaken in the
year, the property tax increment collected, expenses, and projected property tax increment for the
coming year. The report also states the date and time of the public hearing.

Additionally, per the Reimbursement Agreement between the City and the PFA, the initial projects are
being funded by the City, primarily utilizing Prop. C funds. Since they have not yet been realized by the
PFA, these expenses are not shown on the PFA’s annual report, but staff felt that it was important to
document these expenses for the PFA’s benefit. In Fiscal Year 2021-2022 the estimated expenses,
paid with Prop. C funds, for the Pedestrian Bride and E and 2nd Street improvements is $65,000.

Most of these funds were utilized for the design work for the associated projects, with the upcoming
bond issuance used primarily for the E and 2nd Street construction and other improvements along Arrow
Highway. The total cost of the Pedestrian Bridge is expected to be supplemented by multiple other
sources, including a Federal earmark and Measure M sub-regional funding. These projects are all listed
in the Infrastructure Financing Plan (IFP) and while originally expected to be funded fully through the
EIFD, any ability to offset these costs with other funding sources will be explored first.
 The details of the Bond Issuance structure is detailed in the agenda report to the City Council on June
6, 2022 and attached for the PFA’s reference.

Prepared By: Eric Scherer, AICP, Community Development Director

   2021-2022
  Annual Report of the City of La Verne
  Public Financing Authority for the
  Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District

This Annual Report is issued in accordance with the requirements of the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District
Law. The Authority has entered into a reimbursement agreement with the City in order to fund street improvements on
E and 2nd Streets. The City is responsible for these costs initially, with the Authority being responsible to repay those
expenses once the fund balance can support the repayment. Similarly, design work has begun on the Pedestrian Bridge,
but the costs associated with this project are being paid by the San Gabriel Valley Council of Government using Measure
M dollars and the City’s Prop. C fund. Thus, there is no direct fiscal costs for these projects to the District.

  A. Projects Undertaken in Fiscal Year 2021-2022:
  Pedestrian Bridge Design (no direct cost)
  E and 2nd Street Improvements (no direct cost this fiscal year).

  B. Revenues and Expenses for 2021-2022:
  Property Tax Increment:  Fund Balance on 7/1/2021:  $89,700
  Projected 2021-2022 Revenue:  $65,000
  Projected Fund Balance on 6/30/2022: $154,700
  Expenses: $1,300

  C. Amount of Property Tax Increment Projected to be Received for Fiscal Year 2022-2023:
  $75,000

  D. Revenues expended for Housing:
  None to date.

  E. Assessment of completion of Projects in Fiscal Year 2021-2022:
  No projects expected to be completed in this reporting period.

  F. Amount of Revenue expended to assist private businesses:
  None to date.

A public hearing on this annual report will be held before the Public Financing Authority on Wednesday, June 8, 2022
at 9:00 a.m. The meeting will be live streamed at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream and further instructions on how to
participate in the meeting will be posted with the agenda at least 72 hours prior to the meeting at
www.cityoflaverne.org. This report is also available on the dedicated EIFD page at www.cityoflaverne.org/EIFD.

Should you have any questions regarding this report, please email planning@cityoflaverne.org or 909-596-8706.
